## Findings by module

### 7

- **contradicted** (ch-001 chunk 1 (abstract, intro: the linear chain)): Chirikure et al. 2014 (PLOS ONE): the standard chain K2 (CE 1000-1200), Mapungubwe (CE 1220-1290), Great Zimbabwe (CE 1300-1450), Khami (CE 1450-1820) is called a linear orthodoxy; Mapela Hill, south-western Zimbabwe, has prestige stone-walled terraces from the 11th century and fired dhaka floors with K2 pottery and glass beads, flourishing CE 1055-1400, so the Zimbabwe culture was not born only at Mapungubwe. The course lesson 1 table treats Mapungubwe then Great Zimbabwe as a sequence with Huffman-revised dates: show the polycentric alternative as a competing model. Paper gives Great Zimbabwe CE 1300-1450; Reader 1275-1550; course 12th-15th centuries.
- **extended** (ch-001 chunk 2 (Bayesian dates, glass beads, size)): Paper: Bayesian model (OxCal, SHCal13) puts K2 start 1055-1219 cal CE (median 1165), K2 to Transitional K2 1163-1224, Transitional K2 to Mapungubwe 1223-1272; over a thousand glass beads from one terrace; Mapela is larger than K2 and Mapungubwe; no gold found yet (looting possible). Authors argue Mapungubwe may have copied Mapela. Gives the course's Module 7 lesson 1 a dated, tested polycentric alternative; the paper's own limits: nine dates from one trench, Garlake's older dates too uncertain to use. Tag [CONTESTED].
- **extended** (ch-001 chunk 3 (polycentric model, conclusion)): Paper's argument: with many chronologically overlapping Leopard's Kopje sites (Mapela, Malumba, Halisupi, Mapungubwe, later Great Zimbabwe, Khami), it is not possible to name the first palace or first dhaka floor, and early state formation was networked and multiple, as in Sumer and the Maya, and followed demographic growth after CE 900. Mutapa chiefdoms rotated kingship and capitals, so dating a capital by radiocarbon is hard. Use as the competing model in Module 7 lesson 1; the paper is a single-site Bayesian case plus an interpretive framework (actor-network theory), so tag [CONTESTED].
